newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court remands cash courier in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court remands cash courier in scandal.

text.p: A Turkish court has remanded in custody a drug money courier linked by the media to a scandal over alleged ties between authorities and organised crime, court officials said on Tuesday.
Istanbul state security court remanded Dilek Ornek, 22, on Monday after she was detained on December 16 carrying $264,000 in a suitcase on arrival at the city's airport from Amsterdam.
"The girl courier has been questioned and remanded," a court official told Reuters. A policeman detained on suspicion of aiding her was released by the court, he said.
The Turkish press has said other security officials may have helped Ornek ferry cash regularly to Istanbul from the sale of Turkish drugs in the Netherlands and Spain.
Ornek, an ethnic Turk who holds a Dutch passport, has admitted to making more than 50 similar trips with suitcases full of money this year alone, the press has said.

The Islamist-led government has been rocked for almost two months by allegations that Turkey used far-right gangsters to carry out political dirty work in exchange for ignoring their drug-smuggling and money-laundering activities.
The scandal came to light when a car carrying a government MP, a convicted heroin smuggler and a senior policeman crashed in a fatal accident on November 3.
